svg.aria-label: Why a hired seat cannot be a pattern worker, drawn as two lanes against time with one request bracketed on the upper lane. The upper lane is headed one request, and inside the request bracket sits a sequencer holding a coordinator block and three worker blocks, each labelled as a block definition. The whole lane starts when the turn starts and ends when the turn ends, and a note says everything here dies with the reply. The lower lane is headed the roster, and holds three seats drawn as separate rounded shapes, each labelled as a flow instance addressed by its own request, and each seat's line runs the full width of the figure and past both edges, because a seat outlives any one turn. Between the two lanes runs a solid horizontal boundary. One arrow attempts to cross it, from a seat on the lower lane up into the worker slot on the upper lane; it is drawn struck through and labelled as the bridge this design refuses, with the reason beside it: a pattern factory's worker slot takes a block definition, while hiring a workforce returns flow instances, so making a seat fit means wrapping it into something that starts and ends inside one request, which collapses a durable multi-session roster into an in-process loop. A caption at the foot states the consequence that makes this a product decision rather than a typing detail: the two shapes answer at different times, one inside the turn and one on a later turn, so no substitution is invisible to the person reading the screen.
svg.text: sequencer · starts with the turn, ends with the reply
everything here dies with the reply
addressed by its own request · outlives every turn
the bridge this design refuses — a worker slot takes a BlockDefinition,
hireWorkforce returns FlowInstance[]; making one fit ends it inside the turn
The lifetimes are the decision, not the types. Above the line the answer arrives inside the turn; below it, on a later one.
So there is no substitution a reader cannot see — which is why the five routes are removed rather than rebuilt on seats.
